subject.title: [Feature]: Per-session activity state (busy/idle + awaiting_user, awaiting_subagent) via gateway API + WS statechange

question: Should OpenClaw make per-session activity and attention state a first-class Gateway API/WS contract now, and if so which scope should be accepted for the initial implementation?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the requested behavior sets public protocol semantics for activity, attention durability, stale runs, and cross-agent child relationships rather than a narrow bug repair.

options.title: Sponsor the core Gateway contract
options.body: Accept the issue as the canonical design item and review or replace the open implementation PRs against the full RPC, WS, attention, stale-run, and child-rollup contract.

options.title: Narrow to visible liveness only
options.body: Limit the near-term work to `sessions.list` or Control UI live/stale indicators and leave explicit attention and child-rollup semantics for a later design.

options.title: Defer activity API design
options.body: Keep existing liveness flags and close or defer overlapping PRs until a maintainer is ready to own a stable Gateway activity protocol.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core Gateway contract
recommendation.body: Accept the issue as the canonical design item and review or replace the open implementation PRs against the full RPC, WS, attention, stale-run, and child-rollup contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main Gateway session method blame and the live issue assignment both point to this as the best available routing candidate.
